__BUDGET_TABLE__

Rendered from the manifest at generation time - not a live query. See **Ingestion Budget Usage** alongside for the live percentage.

panels.title: Ingestion Budget Usage (per Signal)
panels.description: This tenant's real ingested volume since local midnight (Europe/Zurich), as a percentage of EACH signal's own daily budget - Metrics (Mimir), Logs (Loki), Traces (Tempo), Profiles (Pyroscope) each shown as its own line. Both values read directly from two gauges scripts/ingestion-midnight-snapshot.py pushes every 2 minutes (demo_ingestion_since_midnight, demo_ingestion_daily_budget) - no subtraction on this panel's own side (NFR-05 SECOND pre-test audit round, fixed here: this used to recompute "current minus a separately-pushed day-start snapshot" in this panel's OWN PromQL, independently of - and able to silently disagree with - the enforcer's own decision, with its own version of that script's pre-fix reset-insensitivity; both now read the exact same, already-correct value). Green below 80%, yellow 80-90%, red above 90%. Same formula as the Operator: Tenant Ingestion Budget dashboard's own panel, filtered to this one tenant. Queried via the Mimir-anonymous datasource, not __DATASOURCE_MIMIR__ - see README.md's Multi-Tenancy section for why (self-monitoring metrics land under the anonymous tenant).

panels.title: Request Rate by Endpoint/Operation
panels.description: traces_spanmetrics_calls_total, generated automatically by Tempo's metrics-generator from real spans - no separate app instrumentation needed for this panel. Fixed 5m rate window, not $__rate_interval - found live that Mimir returns empty results for sum/max-by aggregations over a short rate() window on some high-cardinality metrics (likely a query-sharding edge case), even though the bare unaggregated rate() works fine at any window size.

panels.title: Request Latency (p95) by Endpoint/Operation
panels.description: Also derived automatically from real spans via traces_spanmetrics_latency_bucket.

panels.title: Recent Traces
panels.description: A table, not the "traces" panel type - Grafana's traces panel silently renders zero rows when Tempo's search response omits durationMs (happens for very fast, sub-millisecond traces), even though the underlying data is there. A table shows the same rows regardless.
